description: This line plot illustrates the relationship between initial confidence and three accuracy metrics—Initial Accuracy, Final Accuracy, and Δ Accuracy—for a large language model’s response to external feedback, as studied in the paper “Feedback Friction: LLMs Struggle to Fully Incorporate External Feedback.” The x-axis, labeled “Initial Confidence,” spans from approximately 0.87 to 1.00 on a linear scale, with tick marks at intervals of 0.01. The y-axis, labeled “Accuracy,” ranges from 0.0 to 1.0, also on a linear scale, with major gridlines every 0.2. The “Initial Accuracy” (green dashed line with square markers) begins near 0.65 at an initial confidence of 0.87, rises steadily to a peak of approximately 0.92 at 0.98, then drops sharply to about 0.85 at 1.00. The “Final Accuracy” (blue solid line with circle markers) starts near 0.98 at 0.87, increases gradually to about 0.995 at 0.98, and remains near that level at 1.00. The “Δ Accuracy” (orange dashed line with diamond markers) begins around 0.32 at 0.87, dips slightly to 0.30 at 0.90, rises to a peak of approximately 0.48 at 0.92, then declines to 0.40 at 0.94 before climbing again to 0.85 at 1.00. Error bars are present for all three lines, indicating variability in the measurements.
